description: An in-place edit extractor that models an option GRAMMAR in one regex misses the ordinary spellings of its own verb. `_SED_INPLACE_RE`'s optional backup-extension group did double duty: with GNU `-i` it happened to consume the script so the capture landed on the file, but with BSD/macOS `-i ''` it consumed the `''`, and the expression-skip that followed handled only QUOTED scripts -- so an unquoted script was captured as the target and the real file was never checked against the protected zone. A glued `-i.bak` left no whitespace for the backup arm and did not match the pattern at all. `perl`, which spells the same idiom with a different verb, had no arm in `_candidate_paths_from_bash` at any point, so an in-place perl edit to `.claude/settings.json` was plan-gated but NOT protected-zone-gated. THE POPULATION IS DERIVED, WHICH IS THE POINT: the reporting review listed 14 spellings by hand; built as a cross-product over primitives (pre-flag run x in-place spelling x script delivery x target count) and driven at the live hook with maintenance cleared, 237 of 333 sed spellings and 37 of 37 perl spellings reached a protected path unchecked -- the hand roster was 5% of the truth. The fix is a tokenizer (`iter_inplace_edit_targets`) following the in-repo `iter_rm_invocations` precedent, running in UNION with the retained regex so no previously-denied spelling can regress. Its profile table is keyed PER VERB because the grammars genuinely diverge: perl has no bare-script slot (absent `-e`/`-E` its first non-option token is a script FILE, so inheriting sed's positional rule makes `perl -i '' <protected>` swallow the protected file itself as the script -- a silent fail-open with the same shape as the original bug), and perl's `-i` suffix is glued-only where BSD sed's is separable. Attempts below span the four independent failure axes: the BSD separable form with an unquoted script (a1), a glued backup suffix that matched nothing (a2), bundled short flags with a flag preceding `-i` (a3), and the absent perl verb against a second protected zone (a4). Out of scope and deliberately not claimed: `ruby -pi`, `gawk -i inplace`, `awk -i inplace`, `ex -sc` and `sponge` share the idiom and remain ALLOW -- all measured, all with zero uses in this repo and two not installed (STANDING_PRINCIPLES §16), each one table row AND one entry in `_INPLACE_VERB_ALT` away if a user appears -- both, not just the table row; a profile added without the alternation entry is silently inert, which `TestTheVerbSetsCannotDiverge` now pins.
documented_in: tests/test_write_guard_sed_grammar.py::TestTheDerivedPopulationIsExtracted (in-place option-grammar tokenizer over a derived spelling population)
